Its 220 projected users mean sacrificing reach compared with A and C, but I prioritize year-round accessibility and sustained study and digital support. Staff coordination is a genuine delivery risk; I accept it over sports’ weather and accessibility limitations and the garden’s slower benefits and reliance on sustained volunteers.

posts.content: I recommend C, the community growing garden. Its projected 300 users exceed B’s, while food-growing skills, social connection and environmental benefits offer lasting value. A reaches more people immediately, and B offers explicit accessibility advantages. C’s slow progress and volunteer dependence are real risks, but I judge its combination of reach and longer-term benefits worth backing.

I still recommend B, the accessible learning room. C’s skills and environmental benefits are appealing, but depend on sustained volunteer maintenance. A reaches more residents, yet weather and accessibility limit delivery. At the same £30,000 annual cost, B’s 220 projected users and staff-coordination demands are tradeoffs I accept for year-round accessible study and digital support.

I recommend B, the accessible learning room. Its 220 projected users are fewer than A’s 400 or C’s 300, but year-round accessible study and digital support offer sustained value. Staff coordination remains a delivery risk; I accept it over A’s weather and accessibility limitations and C’s slower, volunteer-dependent benefits at the same annual cost.

I recommend B, the accessible learning room. A’s 400 projected users and C’s 300 exceed B’s 220, but I prioritize year-round accessibility and lasting study and digital support. Staff coordination is a real delivery risk; at the same annual budget, I accept it over weather-dependent, less accessible sports or the garden’s slow, volunteer-dependent benefits.

I recommend B, the accessible learning room. Its 220 projected users trail sports’ 400 and the garden’s 300, but year-round accessibility and continuing study and digital support matter more to me. Ongoing staff coordination is a genuine risk; I accept it over sports’ weather and accessibility limitations and the garden’s slower, volunteer-dependent benefits at the same budget.

I recommend B, the accessible learning room. Its 220 projected users mean sacrificing reach compared with A and C, but I prioritize year-round accessibility and sustained study and digital support. Staff coordination is a genuine delivery risk; I accept it over sports’ weather and accessibility limitations and the garden’s slower benefits and reliance on sustained volunteers.

sql: BEGIN TRANSACTION;

CREATE TABLE comment (
    comment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    post_id INTEGER,
    user_id INTEGER,
    content TEXT,
    created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    num_likes INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    num_dislikes INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    FOREIGN KEY(post_id) REFERENCES post(post_id),
    FOREIGN KEY(user_id) REFERENCES user(user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE comment_dislike (
    comment_dislike_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    user_id INTEGER,
    comment_id INTEGER,
    created_at DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY(user_id) REFERENCES user(user_id),
    FOREIGN KEY(comment_id) REFERENCES comment(comment_id)
);

CREATE TABLE comment_like (
    comment_like_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    user_id INTEGER,
    comment_id INTEGER,
    created_at DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY(user_id) REFERENCES user(user_id),
    FOREIGN KEY(comment_id) REFERENCES comment(comment_id)
);

CREATE TABLE dislike (
    dislike_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    user_id INTEGER,
    post_id INTEGER,
    created_at DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY(user_id) REFERENCES user(user_id),
    FOREIGN KEY(post_id) REFERENCES tweet(post_id)
);

CREATE TABLE follow (
    follow_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    follower_id INTEGER,
    followee_id INTEGER,
    created_at DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY(follower_id) REFERENCES user(user_id),
    FOREIGN KEY(followee_id) REFERENCES user(user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE group_members (
    group_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    agent_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    joined_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    PRIMARY KEY (group_id, agent_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (group_id) REFERENCES chat_group(group_id)
);

CREATE TABLE group_messages (
    message_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    group_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    sender_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    content TEXT NOT NULL,
    sent_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    FOREIGN KEY (group_id) REFERENCES chat_group(group_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (sender_id) REFERENCES user(agent_id)
);

CREATE TABLE like (
    like_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    user_id INTEGER,
    post_id INTEGER,
    created_at DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY(user_id) REFERENCES user(user_id),
    FOREIGN KEY(post_id) REFERENCES tweet(post_id)
);

CREATE TABLE mute (
    mute_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    muter_id INTEGER,
    mutee_id INTEGER,
    created_at DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY(muter_id) REFERENCES user(user_id),
    FOREIGN KEY(mutee_id) REFERENCES user(user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE post (
    post_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    user_id INTEGER,
    original_post_id INTEGER,  -- NULL if this is an original post
    content TEXT DEFAULT '',  -- DEFAULT '' for initial posts
    quote_content TEXT,  -- NULL if this is an original post or a repost
    created_at DATETIME,
    num_likes INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    num_dislikes INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    num_shares INTEGER DEFAULT 0,  -- num_shares = num_reposts + num_quotes
    num_reports INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    FOREIGN KEY(user_id) REFERENCES user(user_id),
    FOREIGN KEY(original_post_id) REFERENCES post(post_id)
);
